corrections.detail: On Oct. 2, 2026, we edited the wording on a price-target card for Mark Lipacis (Evercore ISI) on Nvidia (NVDA), dated Nov. 26, 2025, to remove a rating word not used by the broker. Our rules require an analyst's rating to appear in the broker's own published wording. The word came from a third-party summary rather than from Evercore ISI's own wording, so we removed it. The price target ($352) and the deadline (Nov. 27, 2026) are unchanged, and no grade changed. The card is still Pending. We also removed Mark Lipacis's separate rating card on Nvidia today (see the separate entry). This affects only this card and Mark Lipacis's profile.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we edited the wording on a price-target card for Joseph Quatrochi (Wells Fargo) on Applied Materials (AMAT), dated May 27, 2025, to remove a rating word not used by the broker. Our rules require an analyst's rating to appear in the broker's own published wording. The word came from a third-party summary rather than from Wells Fargo's own wording, so we removed it. The price target ($200) and the deadline (May 27, 2026) are unchanged, and no grade changed. The deadline has passed and the card is still Pending. We also removed Joseph Quatrochi's separate rating card on Applied Materials today (see the separate entry). This affects only this card and Joseph Quatrochi's profile.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we edited the wording on a price-target card for Stacy Rasgon (Bernstein) on Intel (INTC), dated Sept. 21, 2026, to remove a rating word not used by the broker. Our rules require an analyst's rating to appear in the broker's own published wording. The word came from a third-party summary rather than from Bernstein's own wording, so we removed it. The edit did not change the price target, the deadline (Sept. 21, 2027) or the grade, and the card was still Pending at the time. Later today we removed this card because its source can't be used under our source rules (see the separate entry). We also removed Stacy Rasgon's separate rating card on Intel today (see the separate entry). This affects only this card and Stacy Rasgon's profile.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we corrected the date said on a price-target card for Christopher Rolland (Susquehanna) on Broadcom: "Rolland (Susquehanna): Positive; raises Broadcom PT to $450 from $400." The card showed Dec. 4, 2025, the day the article says the analyst acted. Our rule is that the date said on an analyst card is the date the article we cite was published, New York time, which here is Dec. 8, 2025. A 12-month price-target deadline counts from that date and moves to the next trading day if needed, so the deadline moved from Dec. 4, 2026 to Dec. 8, 2026. The card is still Pending, and its wording, price target ($450) and source are unchanged. This affects only this card and Christopher Rolland's profile.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we corrected the date said on a rating card for Christopher Rolland (Susquehanna) on Broadcom: "Rolland (Susquehanna): Positive on Broadcom." The card showed Dec. 4, 2025, the day the article says the analyst acted. Our rule is that the date said on an analyst card is the date the article we cite was published, New York time, which here is Dec. 8, 2025. The card is Unscorable, so no grade changed. Its wording and source are unchanged. This affects only this card and Christopher Rolland's profile.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we withdrew 15 daily rainfall totals for Central Park in New York City that we had listed as official results. Each total was a sum we worked out ourselves from the National Weather Service's individual readings during the day. It was not an official daily figure published by the weather service, so it does not meet our rule that results must be official. The withdrawn totals are for Aug. 27, 28, 30 and 31 and Sept. 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, 13, 16, 17, 20, 21 and 22, 2026. No card uses any of these results, so no cards were affected and no grades changed.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we changed the source link for the official result of the 2025 Heisman Trophy (won by Fernando Mendoza) on 9 cards. To fit our rules on which sources we can use, the result now links to Indiana University Athletics' report of the award. The result itself is unchanged, so no grades changed. All 9 cards are still graded Miss. This affects only these cards.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we added back three National Weather Service forecasts of the daily high temperature in Central Park that our duplicate check had wrongly skipped, because their wording matched an earlier forecast for a different day. They are the forecasts issued Sept. 10, 2026, for Sept. 15 (a high near 82°F) and Sept. 16 (a high near 85°F), and the forecast issued Sept. 17, 2026, for Sept. 18 (a high near 80°F). Each keeps its original issue time, and our saved copies show we collected them before the day they cover.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we corrected the issue times on 49 National Weather Service forecasts for Central Park that we collected on Sept. 4 and Sept. 21–23, 2026. We had recorded the time the weather service's server prepared the copy we downloaded instead of the time the forecast itself was last updated. Each now shows the weather service's own update time, about 3½ to 5½ hours earlier. Forecast values, deadlines and grades are unchanged.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we corrected the official result for U.S. real GDP growth in 2025 from 2.0% to 2.2%. The 2.0% we had listed was not the official first-release figure. The corrected result is the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis's first published estimate (GDP Advance Estimate, 4th Quarter and Year 2025, released Feb. 20, 2026), measured from the fourth quarter of 2024 to the fourth quarter of 2025. This affects four Federal Reserve (FOMC) median projections for 2025 growth, made in March 2025 (1.7%), June 2025 (1.4%), September 2025 (1.6%) and December 2025 (1.7%). All four are still misses; only how far off each one was has changed. This affects only these four cards and the FOMC's profile.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we changed the source link for the official result of U.S. PCE inflation in 2025 (fourth quarter of 2024 to fourth quarter of 2025) on 4 cards. To fit our rules on which sources we can use, the result now links to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis's first published estimate (GDP Advance Estimate, 4th Quarter and Year 2025, released Feb. 20, 2026). The result itself is unchanged at 2.8%, so no grades changed. The 4 cards are Federal Reserve (FOMC) median projections made in March, June, September and December 2025, and all 4 are still graded Miss. This affects only these cards.

On Oct. 2, 2026, we changed the source link for the official result of the federal funds rate at the end of 2025 on 4 cards. To fit our rules on which sources we can use, the result now links to the Federal Reserve Board's policy announcement of Dec. 10, 2025. The result itself is unchanged at 3.6% (the midpoint of the 3.50% to 3.75% target range), so no grades changed. The 4 cards are Federal Reserve (FOMC) median projections made in March, June, September and December 2025. The September and December projections are still graded Hit, and the March and June projections are still graded Miss. This affects only these cards.
